features.entryOwner: Standalone jimi-2026.html only. SceneDirector owns one active transition and one latest request. Canonical production entry remains unchanged. Main owns one retained Home, Hub and Beach DOM plus temporary detail.
features.exitOwner: Director retires handles after incoming commit; failures restore outgoing. Epoch and AbortSignal prevent stale completion. Nonpersisted pagehide disposes; visibility and persisted pagehide cancel finite work, pageshow resumes committed state or bootstraps Home.
features.resourcePolicy: Original assets unchanged. Only cold selected Beach builds incrementally, one complete Unit per lifecycle-owned cancellable task; a partial/stale assembly is never cached. Cold scene image readiness is bounded and cancellable; completed roots skip warm traversal. Retained DOM is not a GPU-residency guarantee. No Pixi, game manager, save writes or native synchronization from the separate build.
features.animationPolicy: Finite GSAP motion animates plain numeric poses using the canonical profile; the presentation lease alone writes Unit transform/opacity, with no CSSPlugin DOM targets or layout hydration. Cleanup removes owned wrapper styles directly; hidden Home panels are excluded. Nested artwork/flip transforms remain independent. Opt-in bounded route diagnostics separate setup/build phases, asynchronous waits and RAF gaps, never GPU FPS; passive input diagnostics never change gestures. A diagnostic image-paint toggle leaves nodes/assets/layout intact and defaults to original art ON. Exact choreography parity and first-frame behavior remain acceptance work.
features.audioPolicy: Isolated acceptance slice is explicitly silent; existing game audio unchanged. Canonical feature-specific cues must be integrated before production replacement.
features.hapticPolicy: No haptic source in the isolated slice; accepted production haptics unchanged and migration remains required.
features.visibilityPolicy: One root visibility/input owner, hidden inert preparation, old root hidden before incoming reveal. Main snapshots scroll before visible hide/detach and restores it after reattachment before enter; repeated already-visible rollback preserves current scroll. Beach motion admits conservative viewport/overflow envelopes once per enter/exit; offscreen artwork stays mounted and static, never culled or hidden. Header remains admitted. Input gated through incoming completion. Background and BFCache suspend finite motion.
features.physicalAcceptance: INCOMPLETE prototype, not fluidity acceptance or finished migration. First slice Home/Hub/Beach/card preview only; no canonical save/game integration or Forest/Area55 activation yet. Simulator measurements and visual parity required; phone installation prohibited until user acceptance. The existing three-fives no-Fail incident remains unresolved.

features.entryOwner: JourneyBoardsManager parks existing Worlds 1/2/3 for gameplay only. Hub/Homepage paint parking is rejected: the body-level gameplay cover obscures the runtime z-index 1 Homepage. Cold Hub preparation never installs a cover; warm Hub retains hidden DOM only. For admitted Worlds an opaque sibling cover is installed before paintable styles or clearing inline important hiding; existing suspension retires animation, FX, audio and input before settling a static pose.
features.exitOwner: The exact Collectibles visible-enter owner keeps the covered viewport through both scheduled reveal boundaries and releases its cover in the same task as starting visible animation; terminal destinations retain their validated cover-commit path. Full manager cleanup and Home/Arcade/loader routes retire parking unconditionally. Replacement hides the previous owner before releasing its cover.
features.resourcePolicy: One existing World DOM subtree, one small cover element, no copied assets, derived bitmaps, timers, observers or new renderer. A stable viewport transform layer survives the covered return; permanent retirement removes its marker. No additional Beach main-image promotion hint. GPU paint residency remains an experimental measurement target, not a guarantee of backing or smoothness.
features.animationPolicy: Park is synchronous and silent: current timelines and idle are stopped, known final poses restored under the cover. The existing authored enter owns visible motion. No animation starts during gameplay parking.
features.audioPolicy: No new audio. Existing gameplay suspension retires Journey sessions.
features.hapticPolicy: No new haptics; existing accepted interactions unchanged.
features.visibilityPolicy: Parked World is inert and aria-hidden, below an opaque viewport cover and gameplay surface. Homepage must never retain this cover. The cover is committed before paintable styles and removed only after destination is hidden-primed. Matching element ownership prevents stale release; visual pixels, not accessibility element existence alone, must prove Homepage visibility.
features.physicalAcceptance: Experimental and unaccepted. Must prove restored Homepage pixels through repeated Hub/Home returns, no uncovered flash, no hidden input/idle, preserved scroll/card/save and repeated Simulator worst-frame improvement across all three World returns. No physical installation authorized.

features.entryOwner: JourneyBoardsManager compiles a detached, scoped Beach destination after image readiness and before the existing enter-prime owner. Validation is all-or-nothing; other Worlds retain their current renderer pending the acceptance slice.
features.exitOwner: The existing JourneyWorldAnimationCoordinator and selected-area transition owner animate one structural root, never both root and descendants. Existing stage retirement releases the complete subtree.
features.resourcePolicy: Reparents existing images/cards without copying assets, creating textures, reading live geometry or adding caches. Layout is compiled once from authored coordinates and loaded image dimensions. Retained gameplay return keeps these exact roots; card progression reconciliation preserves local placement.
features.animationPolicy: One bounded Unit root owns enter/exit/vertical idle; cloud leaves keep only independent horizontal idle. Existing duration/ease/sound scheduling remains canonical. Static positions and card interaction listeners remain on the original nodes. No new scheduler or renderer.
features.audioPolicy: Existing Journey Unit cues and sessions unchanged.
features.hapticPolicy: Existing card and navigation interaction owners unchanged.
features.visibilityPolicy: Compilation is detached only. Existing stage token, hidden-surface suspension and coordinator interruption own presentation and cleanup. Scene roots remain noninteractive; existing cards and interim hit owners receive input.
features.physicalAcceptance: Experimental Beach acceptance slice, NOT accepted as fluid. Requires Simulator composition/depth, card interaction and repeated game/result return plus worst-frame comparison before expansion. Physical phone remains prohibited pending user acceptance.

features.entryOwner: JourneyBoardsManager schedules canonical Hub exit synchronously and prepares only the selected destination. Homepage reveal joins Hub image readiness, never three full Worlds. JourneyStageController owns generation-checked stable-node transfer; JourneyRouteTransitionCoordinator owns the foreground presentation lease through incoming completion.
features.exitOwner: Authored exits settle before atomic transfer. The manager retires outgoing runtime/input owners. Full cleanup releases all retained surfaces. Pressure evicts optional inactive Worlds but protects the accepted destination and never disables Hub admission.
features.resourcePolicy: One Hub plus at most one retained World. A different cold destination first releases the previous inactive World. Construction, image readiness and enter priming stay detached until atomic commit; no full-alpha connected preparation or paint-frame barrier. Gameplay parks the live World. Homepage parks an existing Hub through the same idempotent suspension owner before Home enters; the next Hub entry resumes its lifecycle and refreshes canonical progression without replacing its nodes. An unexpected World on the Home exit still receives full cleanup. No new assets or caches; DOM retention does not imply GPU residency.
features.animationPolicy: Existing canonical timing, Unit grouping and enter/exit owners remain unchanged. Every retained destination receives its hidden enter pose before reveal. The accepted tap reaches the canonical selected and sibling Hub exit in the same task. No new ticker; inactive runtimes remain retired and only the current surface reactivates. The route coordinator lease covers outgoing motion through complete incoming presentation and releases on completion, interruption and cleanup.
features.audioPolicy: Existing navigation and Journey cue owners unchanged; no new sound source or transport.
features.hapticPolicy: Existing accepted interaction and animation callbacks unchanged.
features.visibilityPolicy: Preparation never writes screen-root visibility. Gameplay suspension keeps its World inert and hidden. Return restores that same World using token and generation checks. Memory pressure can cancel optional plans, not delete a parked World. Stale events and cleanup cannot acquire a replacement route.
features.physicalAcceptance: NEEDS PHYSICAL TEST: repeated Hub/World/card/game/result routes, immediate scroll and interrupted return, cold versus warm worst-frame comparison, bounded memory and sustained thermal behavior on iPhone 13 blue. Source identity/work-count tests do not establish mobile smoothness.

features.entryOwner: Existing gameplay-return receipt and origin lease admit one automatic reminder; stage mounts before validating the portal clone.
features.exitOwner: Existing idempotent reminder cleanup handles completion, replacement, World X, navigation, pagehide and lost anchor, restores the resident card and cancels flight/impact/follow frames.
features.resourcePolicy: Existing card clone and authored back-face preloader; no new assets, caches or decoded resources.
features.animationPolicy: World-owned reminders mount a non-clipping viewport-coordinate absolute plane inside the same scrolling World content. Native plane uses size/layout/style containment, never paint containment or overflow clipping; the real scrollport owns visibility at the fold. Native compositor scrolling moves the Unit and plane together; existing finite follow RAF compensates only Unit-local displacement after subtracting host movement. Fallback without a World retains fixed viewport tracking and viewport clipping. Existing flip, apex, stable landing target, impact and duration remain unchanged; no scroll lock or new timer.
features.audioPolicy: Existing entry-flip sounds retain their trigger and cleanup owner.
features.visibilityPolicy: Origin loss and pagehide retire the presentation; navigation cannot leave a stale portal. Scroll input remains owned by the player.
features.physicalAcceptance: NEEDS PHYSICAL TEST: native iPhone momentum scroll during automatic gameplay-return flip and edge clipping. Browser painted hit-test fixture scripts/fixtures/journey-reminder-clipping.html proves initial-fold clipping removal but not iOS frame pacing.

features.entryOwner: AppZoneManager presentation epoch owns route validity. Hub activation and Fail/Clean Board/manual Exit Game return tokens own one required destination promise. Collectibles joins readiness before commit; no terminal connected-paint lease. Homepage CTA cancels an active enter immediately, invalidating the old return cleanup.
features.exitOwner: Authored exit owners remain authoritative. Replacement cancels old tokens; tracked waits and outer Homepage cleanup check exact ownership. Clean Board transfers its existing static paper after result/board exit; the return coordinator releases it only when the prepared Journey destination is committed. No additional three-frame paint pass.
features.resourcePolicy: Homepage return awaits only its memoized responsive hero set. Required Homepage-to-Hub preparation runs concurrently with outgoing motion; preparation never changes root presentation or performs full-alpha prepaint. One destination World is rendered detached, one main or board Unit per owned turn, and Clean Board admits that optional work only after visible counters settle. Shared finite transform preparation applies known hidden poses without per-target computed-style snapshots or GSAP transform hydration after an accepted tap and yields only when actual writes exceed the measured 4ms budget. It uses the existing stage-owned cancellable presentation turns, retains no cache or timer and checks ownership after every yield. A second foreground-resource lease stays active through the complete incoming Hub/World cascade so optional decode, eviction, prepaint and hidden-renderer work remains suspended; it never wakes hidden Pixi. Board transition and reward images share one globally bounded two-job decoder; stale owners stop admitting queued work. Pressure retires optional preparation without permanently disabling future required construction.
features.animationPolicy: Canonical timings and Unit grouping are unchanged. Detached cold destinations receive their hidden pose before commit. Parked Worlds reconcile changed cards and normalize retained transforms once. Adopting a prepared return performs no re-render, image traversal or paint wait. Root visibility belongs to the presentation owner; complete enter owns input and idle handoff. Manual Journey exit skips generic post-board RAF/settle barriers.
features.audioPolicy: Existing feature cue owners, sources, gains and triggers remain authoritative. One persistent 4MiB Journey core package protects fifteen short Navigation/CTA, backpack, flip and Hub/Unit-motion cues while Journey is retained; each critical route nests a speculative-load quarantine and headroom-only idle compaction through the complete incoming cascade. Journey cleanup, Sounds OFF and global hard cleanup release the core package. The currently committed Special owns one captured bounded working set and stale decode completion from its replaced family is discarded.
features.hapticPolicy: Existing interaction and authored animation events own haptics.
features.visibilityPolicy: Render generation, cancellation token and presentation epoch reject obsolete completion. Covered Homepage-to-Hub preparation joins displayed-image readiness before reveal. A WeakMap keyed by image node and source/density shares pending/completed readiness with visible enter and Hub prepaint; source replacement invalidates it, failed/unfinished images remain retryable and retired nodes are not retained. A dedicated post-enter owner retires delayed scroll, active-area and idle callbacks on replacement or exit. World/Hub runtime schedulers and manager teardown own hidden/background suspension.
features.physicalAcceptance: NEEDS PHYSICAL TEST: all six surfaces, pressure before and during preparation, rapid return, worst frame, first visible frame, resource growth and sustained thermal behavior. A 4ms slice target cannot preempt one indivisible browser operation.

features.entryOwner: Each presentation has one generation/lifetime owner and rejects stale async completion.
features.exitOwner: Close, navigation, replacement and interruption converge on idempotent owner cleanup.
features.resourcePolicy: Visible cards may use 2x artwork; alpha masks use 1x art. The detail modal retains one shell and binds one dedicated reusable front image/ribbon instead of cloning the connected World card subtree on each open. New Reward mounts its opaque surface immediately while the shared globally bounded two-job image decoder continues underneath, and its crumple playback joins that same preparation rather than delaying first presentation. Special Dice uses the same bounded decoder; Special unlock sources are released on cleanup.
features.animationPolicy: Reveal, shine, shadow and CTA motion are finite. Raw card pointer movement retains only the latest sample and commits at most one compositor paint through the tracked frame owner; pointer release synchronously flushes the latest sample before deciding gesture intent. New Reward reuses the canonical Hub Cartoon Bounce path at 0.8 timing scale: the interim card fully inflates and collapses before the unlocked face begins its faster 0.28s back-out enter; collect uses the same fast inflate-collapse while copy exits concurrently. Reduced Motion skips inflation and uses bounded 0.16s transitions. While the brown question-mark card is visible and unrevealed, its float and 3D tilt run as paired finite three-second WAAPI cycles that re-arm only after both settle; each settled cycle also starts one bounded burn/glow plus shimmer pulse without repeating haptics. The user-required unlocked New Reward coach starts every three seconds and unlocked tilt repeats as finite screen-local bursts through one replaceable timeout each; tap, reveal, drag, close, replacement, background cleanup or disposal cancels the relevant owners.
features.audioPolicy: Feature cues use their dedicated Journey owners and obey Settings plus interruption cleanup. The active detail modal holds one generation-safe atomic flip package lease and releases it on close, replacement or disposal; direct audible play remains immediate.
features.hapticPolicy: Haptics are interaction/event driven and create no polling or idle owner.
features.visibilityPolicy: Hidden, replaced and disposed presentations stop their owned work and cannot resume through stale callbacks.
features.physicalAcceptance: NEEDS PHYSICAL TEST after bundled delivery for sustained thermal behavior, FPS, touch, audio and visual feel.

features.entryOwner: Each existing navigation or clickable HUD control starts the shared tap bounce from its established pointer or click handler without changing its action owner.
features.exitOwner: The shared finite GSAP timeline restores scale on completion; repeat taps replace target tweens, while each screen retains its existing navigation and disposal lifecycle.
features.resourcePolicy: The feedback reuses mounted DOM and Pixi icon visuals and creates no persistent renderer, timer, observer or media resource.
features.animationPolicy: All active navigation and clickable HUD icon feedback uses one bounded 220ms profile: scale 1 to 0.92 to 1.06 to 1 with the former-heart cubic-bezier easing. Semantic gameplay, score and reward animations remain owned by their feature runtimes.
features.audioPolicy: No audio ownership changes; every control keeps its existing navigation, close or feature-specific sound owner.
features.hapticPolicy: No haptic ownership changes; the shared animation creates no haptic trigger.
features.visibilityPolicy: Hidden or removed surfaces cannot receive input; completion normalizes the animated visual and existing screen cleanup remains authoritative.
features.physicalAcceptance: NEEDS PHYSICAL TEST after bundled delivery for tap feel, visual consistency, clipping, touch responsiveness, FPS and thermal behavior.

features.entryOwner: One GameplayRendererSupervisor owns context-restored, foreground/pageshow, prepared gameplay entry, settled-board, Special parity and explicit retry joins for the current renderer generation. Duplicate callers join the same bounded promise instead of starting parallel repair.
features.exitOwner: Gameplay teardown calls retireLifecycle, which invalidates late async completion, clears the fallback and recovery input lock, and keeps the singleton reusable for the next entry. Permanent dispose is reserved for permanent owner destruction.
features.resourcePolicy: The supervisor first rehydrates current-generation core and Special textures through existing asset owners. One failed validation may create one temporary Pixi shell solely as a renderer factory, transplant its hidden renderer and canvas onto the existing Application/stage/model, then dispose the old renderer only after validated reveal. The shared tracked-timeout registry owns every recovery deadline.
features.animationPolicy: Recovery adds no decorative motion or ticker. It stops the existing ticker and frame controllers while unsafe, restarts the established owners after rehydration, and never reveals an intermediate or blank frame.
features.audioPolicy: No audio source or transport is created. Existing gameplay audio ownership is unchanged and recovery does not decode speculative sound families.
features.visibilityPolicy: Stage, board, HUD and canvas remain hidden and the persistent all-input gate remains locked until structural ownership, die semantic parity, current renderer generations, GPU probes and extracted painted pixels all pass. Failure stays fail-visible through the paper fallback; it cannot silently expose a blank board.
features.physicalAcceptance: NEEDS PHYSICAL TEST: reproduce background/foreground, forced WebGL loss, gameplay entry/exit and long mixed play on iPhone 13 blue; verify no blank logical board, no hidden Special, one bounded recovery, responsive fallback, stable FPS and bounded thermal/memory behavior.

features.entryOwner: The guarded core renderer recovery lifecycle may mount one replacement-safe fallback only after a current gameplay renderer recovery fails; the fallback never acquires gameplay or Pixi ownership.
features.exitOwner: Explicit recovery success, confirmed safe route completion, replacement and renderer teardown converge on one idempotent dispose path; stale async action completion cannot remove a newer fallback.
features.resourcePolicy: DOM-only canonical paper surface with no new image decoder, renderer, cache, timer, observer, media or persistent resource.
features.animationPolicy: Static fail-visible presentation with no animation or recurring work. Repeated action input is coalesced until the current action settles.
features.audioPolicy: No audio source, cue or transport ownership.
features.visibilityPolicy: The core renderer owner keeps Pixi hidden and the persistent all-input gate locked while recovery is unsafe. Rejected or non-confirming actions keep this opaque actionable surface mounted; only an explicit true result removes it.
features.physicalAcceptance: NEEDS PHYSICAL TEST after app-core wiring: force WebGL recovery failure on iPhone 13 blue, verify the paper fallback is visible above the hidden canvas, gameplay remains locked, Retry can recover, Return reaches a safe route, and repeated failure/retry does not duplicate the surface or leak work.
